summary.tldr: Requires health information technology vendors to make their systems interoperable and bans data blocking, through federal rules that can apply province by province.
what_it_does: Requires health information technology vendors to make the systems they license, sell, or provide as a service interoperable, so users can access, use, and exchange electronic health information.
Prohibits data blocking by vendors, unless the regulations allow a specific practice or act.
Lets the Governor in Council make the Act apply in a province or territory only if that government does not have requirements that are substantially similar to, or stronger than, the federal rules.
Allows regulations to set standards, define data blocking practices, create complaint and review processes, and establish administrative monetary penalties for non-compliance.
Removes the usual Statutory Instruments Act limit on incorporating documents by reference for certain technical standards.
Says section 126 of the Criminal Code does not apply to contraventions of this Act or its regulations.
summary.background: The drafters say the bill is meant to make electronic health information easier to access, use, and exchange, and to keep it secure.
